title: Gideon and the Songbook
premise: Ivo Lockridge inherited Bellhollow Vineyard along with its crushing debts and a silence that has hung over the family for eleven years — ever since his brother Gideon left after a quarrel neither of them will name. When a letter postmarked a decade ago surfaces inside an old songbook, Ivo discovers Gideon wrote to him every year, letters someone intercepted to keep the brothers apart and the vineyard's true ownership hidden. As Ivo follows the trail of the songbook through the small town that raised him, he falls for Marisol Vega, the music teacher who owns it and who carries her own secret about what she knows of the Lockridge family. In the end, Ivo must choose between saving the vineyard by selling out the truth or losing everything to expose the person who stole eleven years from them both — and forgiveness, once given, turns out to be the only harvest worth keeping.
about_author: Jonah Iversen is a former wine-country sommelier who traded tasting notes for love stories set among vines and old family wounds. He writes in the early mornings before the fog lifts, convinced that every small town keeps at least one letter it never meant to deliver.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Rows
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Three years into running Bellhollow Vineyard, Ivo faces another failed harvest and a bank notice he hides from his housekeeper, Rosa. The chapter establishes his debts, his loneliness, and his habit of blaming timing instead of himself. Emotional beat: quiet resignation masking grief over his estranged brother Gideon.

chapters.title: A Songbook with Someone Else's Name
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Music teacher Marisol Vega buys a box of donated books for her classroom and finds a leather songbook inscribed 'G.L.' Inside is a letter, postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to Ivo Lockridge. She hesitates — she knows the Lockridge history better than anyone should. Emotional beat: curiosity tangled with dread.

chapters.title: Eleven Years, Undelivered
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Marisol brings the letter to the vineyard; Ivo recognizes Gideon's handwriting instantly. The letter speaks of a debt forgiven and a door left open. Ivo's hands shake as he realizes more letters may exist. Emotional beat: shock cracking open old guilt.

chapters.title: What Rosa Kept
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He confronts Rosa gently about the years of unopened mail; she admits his late father ordered all of Gideon's correspondence burned — but she saved one box. Inside: nine more letters, each sealed. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as protection, and the first hint their father had something to hide.

chapters.title: Reading Him Back to Life
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, interwoven with letter excerpts. Over three nights Ivo reads Gideon's yearly letters: jokes, apologies, descriptions of a life in Lisbon, and a recurring plea — 'ask Dad about the deed.' Emotional beat: intimacy with a brother he thought he'd lost, and rising unease about the vineyard's ownership.

chapters.title: Chords in the Classroom
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Ivo shows up at the school where Marisol teaches, ostensibly to thank her, really because being alone with the letters is unbearable. She plays the melody written on the songbook's flyleaf; Ivo recognizes it as their mother's lullaby. Emotional beat: unexpected connection, two people orbiting the same wound.

chapters.title: The Deed That Doesn't Add Up
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the county records office, Ivo finds the vineyard's title was transferred to a holding company the same month Gideon left — signed by their father. The bank threatening foreclosure isn't the real owner. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Wine Tasting, Truth Spilling
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marisol helps Ivo host a desperate fundraiser tasting; between pours they trade confessions — her father was the Lockridges' lawyer, and he handled the transfer papers before dying. Emotional beat: attraction deepening alongside the sense that their families are entangled in the same lie.

chapters.title: The Tenth Letter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Letter ten, dated last year, says Gideon is coming home — and names the person he planned to confront. The page is water-damaged; the name is illegible. Emotional beat: hope and fear arriving together, because Gideon may already be nearby.

chapters.title: Rosa's Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV (first time). Rosa recalls the night Gideon left: the shouting, the fire in the study, her father-figure loyalty to old Mr. Lockridge. She reveals the father wasn't protecting the boys — he was protecting himself. Emotional beat: a loyal woman choosing truth at last.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching the Vineyard
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A black sedan appears at the property line twice in one week; the foreman reports a man asking about 'the Lockridge parcel.' Ivo suspects the holding company is moving to take the land before he can contest the deed. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: What Marisol Never Said
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Digging through his father's files, Ivo finds Marisol's father's signature on a second document — a codicil naming Gideon sole heir if he returned within twelve years. Confronting Marisol, he learns she found the codicil months ago and said nothing, afraid it would destroy him. Emotional beat: first rupture between them; loyalty versus truth made personal.

chapters.title: Harvest Without a Brother
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Mid-harvest, understaffed and heartsore, Marisol comes back to help pick grapes anyway. Working rows in silence, then not in silence, they begin repairing what the codicil cracked. Emotional beat: forgiveness practiced in small physical acts.

chapters.title: The Man from Meridian Holdings
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The sedan's driver introduces himself as an agent for Meridian Holdings and offers Ivo a buyout that would clear his debts overnight — with a deadline of thirty days. Ivo notices the agent flinches at Gideon's name. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Lisbon on the Line
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Using the return address from letter ten, Ivo calls a café in Lisbon; Gideon answers. Eleven years of silence collapse into one conversation cut short when Gideon hears someone else breathing on the line and hangs up. Emotional beat: reunion almost grasped, then snatched away.

chapters.title: The Interceptor
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Cross-referencing her father's client ledger with the letters' dates, Marisol identifies who intercepted the mail: Uncle Aldous Lockridge, the father's business partner — now the silent principal behind Meridian Holdings. Emotional beat: horror that the villain was family all along, sitting at every holiday table.

chapters.title: Thirty Days, Twenty-Two Grapes
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. With the buyout deadline looming, Ivo refuses to sign and instead files to contest the deed using the codicil. Aldous retaliates: liens, frozen accounts, a smear story in the local paper. Emotional beat: defiance at great cost; the town begins choosing sides.

chapters.title: Gideon Comes Home
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A bus arrives at the valley crossroads and Gideon Lockridge steps off, older, guarded, carrying the original deed copy he's protected for a decade. The brothers meet in the vineyard at dusk — no speeches, just Gideon picking up a harvest knife and starting work. Emotional beat: reconciliation without absolution yet.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the county courthouse, Aldous produces a forged waiver supposedly signed by Gideon renouncing inheritance. Marisol testifies about the codicil; Rosa produces the burned-letter evidence she hid for years. The judge orders a forensic comparison and grants a stay of sale. Emotional beat: climax — truth on trial, literally.

chapters.title: What Forgiveness Costs
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. On the eve of the ruling, Gideon admits his own sin: he took money from Aldous years ago to stay away, believing Ivo had chosen the vineyard over him. Ivo forgives him anyway — and asks forgiveness for the mirror-image choice he made. Emotional beat: the theme resolved between brothers before the law resolves it on paper.

chapters.title: Bellhollow, Restored
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The court voids the forged waiver and restores the brothers' co-ownership; Meridian collapses under fraud exposure, and Aldous leaves town rather than face charges. The debts are restructured against a genuinely good harvest. Emotional beat: relief earned, not gifted; belonging reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Songbook's Last Page
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At the harvest festival, Gideon gives Marisol the songbook, revealing the final blank pages were meant for new songs. Ivo writes the first line; Marisol sets it to their mother's lullaby; the whole found-family town sings it badly and happily. Final beat: second chances aren't about timing — they're about showing up.
